input: prices is a list of n nonnegative safe integers, 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Its values are successive daily prices. The sum of all positive adjacent-day increases must be <= 9007199254740991. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The maximum integer profit with any number of buy/sell transactions, at most one share held at a time, no transaction fees and no cooldown. Buying and selling on the same day is allowed but adds no profit. Empty or singleton inputs return 0; the method returns profit, not a transaction plan.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Only a running profit and adjacent difference are maintained.
numeric: Each nonnegative price is at most 9007199254740991, so adjacent differences lie within the safe signed range. The sum-of-positive-increases precondition bounds every nondecreasing profit accumulator prefix, not just an unconstrained final net total. All arithmetic is exact on the paired domain.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Summing positive adjacent increases captures every rising segment and never carries losses across falling segments. No sorting, input copy or retained transaction history is used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 273 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline.
